title: Agent ships code or config before trusted evaluation/approval
bad_event: Content is deployed that was not reviewed by a non-stager reviewer, or to a target not approved, or twice under one approval, or after HALT. Read "by X" as "by an operation carrying X's authenticated identity" (credential separation is a premise, not a theorem). Trusted review additionally needs role disjointness between agents and reviewers (no disjoint variant proved yet; REVIEW-PACKET finding 7, witness W4).
adversary: Model: any trace of stage/overwrite/review/approve/deploy/halt operations with arbitrary content (agent-pushable registry).
refutation: A trace that deploys unreviewed content or to an unapproved target despite full checks (Lean witnesses show each check is necessary).
scope: Lean model only; no runtime harness yet. Not: review competence, registry/signing infrastructure.

assumptions.text: Every operation carrying a trusted role's identity (approver, reviewer, admin, auditor, verifier, user) is that principal's own act: agents cannot obtain or forge trusted identities. Not modelled: the Lean models read caller identity as authenticated (REVIEW-PACKET-2026-10-09 finding 1).
Hash is injective on contents in the run (collision resistance).
Deploy through the gate is the only route to the target.
Agent and reviewer/approver identities are disjoint.
